KNW-001.q: What three things does a seed need to grow?

KNW-004.q: What three things does every fire need?

KNW-005.q: Your big sticks won't catch fire. What should you light first?
KNW-005.why: Small dry twigs catch fire easily and then help the bigger sticks burn.

KNW-006.why: A fire needs air, so covering it with soil makes it go out.

The soil burns up like fuel

So the stone stays sharp forever

KNW-015.q: What do we call the long time when people used stone tools?

KNW-151.why: Sand melted in a very hot furnace becomes glass.

KNW-152.q: Why must new glass cool slowly?
KNW-152.why: Cooling too fast can crack glass, so it is cooled slowly.

KNW-153.q: Why put glass in a window?
KNW-153.why: Glass is clear, so light comes in while wind and rain stay out.
answers: It lets light in and keeps rain out
It lets the fresh breeze blow through

KNW-154.q: Why is it warm inside a greenhouse?
KNW-154.why: Sunlight shines in through the glass, and the glass keeps the warm air inside.
answers: Sun warms it and glass keeps heat in
A fire burns under the floor
The plants breathe out lots of hot air

KNW-155.why: Tender plants get hurt by cold, so a greenhouse keeps them safe.
answers: Plants that are soft to eat

KNW-156.q: It is still chilly in early spring. Where can you start seedlings?
KNW-156.why: A greenhouse is warm and bright, just right for young seedlings.

KNW-157.q: Why does each row of bricks overlap the row below?
KNW-157.why: Overlapping, called a bond, ties the bricks together so the wall stays strong.
answers: It makes the wall look red

KNW-158.why: Mortar is a paste that sticks the bricks together and dries hard.

KNW-159.q: Why build with bricks instead of wood?
KNW-159.why: Fired clay bricks can't catch fire or rot like wood can.

KNW-160.why: With more light and air inside, the tree grows better fruit.
answers: To let in light and air

KNW-161.q: When do you prune fruit trees?
KNW-161.why: Fruit trees are pruned in winter, before the spring blossoms come.

KNW-162.q: Who helps the apple blossoms turn into apples?
KNW-162.why: Bees carry pollen between blossoms, which lets apples grow.

KNW-163.q: Why are fresh olives soaked in salty water?
KNW-163.why: Weeks of soaking in salty water, called curing, takes the bitterness away.
answers: They are too bitter to eat
They are too sweet to eat
They are too dry to eat

KNW-164.q: How long can an olive tree live?
KNW-164.why: Olive trees grow slowly and can live for hundreds of years.

KNW-165.q: What do you get when you press olives?
KNW-165.why: Pressing squeezes the oil out of olives.

KNW-166.why: Kneading builds gluten, which makes the dough stretchy.

KNW-167.q: What is pasta dough made from?
KNW-167.why: Pasta needs just flour and eggs, or flour and water.

KNW-168.q: How long does fresh pasta take to cook?
KNW-168.why: Fresh pasta is thin, so boiling water cooks it in minutes.

KNW-169.q: Why make a barrel from oak?
KNW-169.why: Slow-growing hardwoods like oak make heavy, strong wood.
answers: Oak wood is heavy and strong
Oak wood is soft and light

KNW-170.why: Softwoods come from conifers, the trees with needles and cones.

KNW-171.q: Which kind of tree grows faster?
KNW-171.why: Conifers like pine grow faster than hardwoods like oak and beech.

KNW-172.why: Humus forms when old plants rot down into dark soil.

KNW-173.q: How is humus like a sponge?
KNW-173.why: Humus soaks up water and keeps it for plant roots.

KNW-174.q: Why can many plants grow close in deep, humus-rich soil?
KNW-174.why: Deep soil with humus holds lots of water and food for many roots.
answers: There is plenty of water and food
Stones in the soil keep roots warm

KNW-175.why: Under thick mulch, weed seeds get no light, so they can't grow.
answers: It makes the soil too hot
It makes the soil too wet

KNW-176.q: It's a hot, dry week. How does mulch help?
KNW-176.why: Mulch covers the soil like a blanket, so less water dries up.
answers: It keeps water in the soil
It makes rain fall more often

KNW-177.q: What happens to old mulch over time?
KNW-177.why: Mulch slowly rots down and becomes humus that feeds the soil.

KNW-178.q: Which plant gives a blue dye?
KNW-178.why: Woad leaves make a blue dye.

KNW-179.q: You want yellow yarn. What should you boil?
KNW-179.why: Onion skins make a warm yellow dye.

KNW-180.q: Your dyed yarn faded when washed. What did you forget?
KNW-180.why: A mordant fixes the dye, so the colour stays when washed.

KNW-181.q: Which two dye colours make green?
KNW-181.why: Yellow mixed with blue gives green.

KNW-182.q: You mix red and blue dye. What colour do you get?
KNW-182.why: Red and blue together make purple.

KNW-183.q: You pour red, yellow and blue together. What colour now?
KNW-183.why: Mixing all three main colours makes brown.

KNW-184.why: Castings are worm droppings, and they are very rich food for plants.
answers: What worms leave behind after eating
Little worm eggs in the soil

KNW-185.q: How do worm tunnels help your plants?
KNW-185.why: Tunnels make paths for air and water to reach the roots.
answers: They let air and water in
They catch the slugs at night

KNW-186.q: What does a worm bin do with kitchen scraps?
KNW-186.why: Worms eat the scraps and leave castings, a rich food for soil.

KNW-187.q: Which plants should you save seeds from?
KNW-187.why: Seeds from your best plants grow into good plants too.

KNW-188.q: How should you store saved seeds?
KNW-188.why: Cool, dry seeds stay healthy until planting time next year.

KNW-189.q: Why do seed libraries share old seeds?
KNW-189.why: When many people grow old kinds, those plants stay alive for the future.
answers: So old seeds can be thrown away

KNW-190.q: Why does saffron cost so much?
KNW-190.why: About 150 flowers, all picked by hand, make just one gram.
answers: It grows on big, tall trees

KNW-191.q: Which part of the crocus is saffron?
KNW-191.why: Saffron is the three red threads, called stigmas, in each flower.

KNW-192.q: What does a pinch of saffron do to rice?
KNW-192.why: Just a pinch of saffron turns food a golden yellow.

KNW-193.q: Why beat the eggs for a cake?
KNW-193.why: Beaten eggs hold air, which makes the cake light.
answers: To warm them up for the oven

KNW-194.q: Your cake burned outside but stayed raw inside. Why?
KNW-194.why: Steady, gentle heat lets the middle bake before the outside burns.
answers: The eggs were beaten too long

KNW-195.q: How do you make flour fine enough for light cakes?
KNW-195.why: Grinding twice and sifting makes very fine flour for light cakes.
answers: Grind it twice and sift it
Mix in plenty of coarse bran

KNW-196.q: What makes a wind pump work?
KNW-196.why: The wind spins the sails, and that drives the pump.

KNW-197.q: How does a wind pump lift water?
KNW-197.why: The sails move a pump rod up and down, lifting water each time.
answers: A rod moves up and down

KNW-198.q: When does a wind pump fill the tank?
KNW-198.why: It runs whenever there is wind, even at night.

KNW-199.q: How many tiny living things are in a spoonful of healthy soil?
KNW-199.why: Healthy soil is packed with billions of tiny living things.

KNW-200.q: How do fungi help plant roots?
KNW-200.why: Long, thin fungus threads reach far and help roots get water.
answers: Their threads help roots find water
They scare away the slugs and snails

KNW-201.q: How can you keep your soil alive?
KNW-201.why: Compost feeds the soil life, and too much digging disturbs it.
answers: Add compost and dig only a little
Dig it up deeply every single week
